source.title: An integrative model of the maturation of cognitive control.

confidence_rationale: This is the one entry that speaks to ARC-120's DEVELOPMENTAL half rather than its arbitration half, and that is why it is here despite a lower score. It documents that the component computations of cognitive control are present and recruitable in childhood while the ability to CONSISTENTLY exert control arrives much later, tracking signal-to-noise and network specialisation rather than the appearance of the computation. Confidence is limited by the fact that this is a synthesis rather than a test, and that maturation is a substrate story (myelination, dopamine/GABA interaction) that may impose the ordering for reasons unrelated to any authority gate.
failure_signatures: Consistency, not capacity, is what matures -- an architecture that tests a mechanism's competence by whether it CAN produce the right output, rather than whether it does so RELIABLY across contexts, will grant authority far too early.

The maturational ordering is imposed partly by substrate constraints (signal-to-noise, network integration) rather than by an explicit gate, so a system can exhibit ARC-120's sequence without containing any competence-gating mechanism at all -- the sequence is evidence for the principle only where the ordering is enforced rather than merely emergent.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The ability to consistently exert cognitive control improves into adulthood as component processes (inhibitory control, performance monitoring, working memory) become flexibly integrated; unique maturational changes in brain structure, supported by dopaminergic-GABAergic interactions, enhance network synchronisation and signal-to-noise ratio, which in turn drive specialisation and strengthening of the networks supporting adult-level control.
mapping.ree_translation: Empirical support for ARC-120's ordering claim specifically: the component computations EXIST and are recruitable long before the system reliably lets them govern behaviour, and what changes in between is measured competence (consistency, signal-to-noise, integration) rather than the arrival of a new computation. This is the developmental-sequence half of ARC-120 -- existence -> representation -> competence -> authority -- observed in a biological system over years.
mapping.mapping_caveat: An integrative review, not a test of ARC-120; the ordering it documents is at least partly IMPOSED by substrate maturation (myelination, receptor development) rather than ENFORCED by a gate, and ARC-120 asserts a gate. A developmental sequence that emerges from slow hardware is compatible with, but does not demonstrate, an architectural commitment to earning authority. Human developmental neuroimaging and behaviour; no computational substrate.
mapping.source_context: Integrative review of human developmental cognitive neuroscience -- cellular, circuit and systems evidence spanning childhood to adulthood, with adolescence framed as a period of heightened experience-seeking.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality (Annual Review, authoritative group). Mapping_fidelity is the limiting factor: the review demonstrates the ORDERING but not that the ordering is enforced by a competence gate, which is what ARC-120 actually asserts. Transfer risk 0.45 -- human developmental timescales to a computational substrate with no equivalent of myelination or receptor maturation is a long transfer, and the mechanism producing the ordering may not survive it.
